title: Void Ending in a Conjunction with Neptune
source: Picatrix (adapted), Book I chapter 5, Book II chapter 3 and Book III chapter 1

<!-- generated by tools/content/gen-void.ts; edit the generator, not this file -->

The conjunction is the closest bond the Moon makes: at it, her strength takes on the nature of the planet she has joined, and the doctrine of the fifth quality treats her meeting with the Sun as the strongest of all her figures. A course that closes on a conjunction ends in union rather than separation, the Moon's virtue soaked through with the planet's own nature.

When the Moon closes her course in a sign with a conjunction with Neptune, the quiet stretch that follows carries something of his drifting mist. Neptune is unknown to Picatrix; the planet was found in 1846, by calculation before anyone saw it, and the source never mentions it. Any reading of it here is this almanac's extension of the lunar doctrine, not the doctrine itself. Named for the Greek lord of the sea, it is read as cold, blue, and dissolving: a course that closes on it ends in something misty, where edges soften and matters drift rather than conclude.
